problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a series of cargo crates onto identical freight pallets. The crates are labeled as follows:
* Crate Alpha: mass 34kg
* Crate Beta: mass 56kg
* Crate Gamma: mass 42kg
* Crate Delta: mass 41kg
* Crate Epsilon: mass 43kg
* Crate Zeta: mass 47kg
* Crate Eta: mass 53kg
* Crate Theta: mass 63kg
* Crate Iota: mass 58kg
* Crate Kappa: mass 58kg
* Crate Lambda: mass 69kg
* Crate Mu: mass 56kg
* Crate Nu: mass 43kg
* Crate Xi: mass 64kg
* Crate Omicron: mass 58kg
* Crate Pi: mass 51kg
* Crate Rho: mass 36kg
* Crate Sigma: mass 43kg
* Crate Tau: mass 69kg
* Crate Upsilon: mass 60kg
* Crate Phi: mass 49kg
* Crate Chi: mass 67kg
* Crate Psi: mass 36kg
* Crate Omega: mass 31kg
* Crate Asterisk: mass 32kg
* Crate Ampersand: mass 34kg
* Crate Section: mass 44kg
* Crate Paragraph: mass 65kg
* Crate Bracket: mass 57kg
* Crate Caret: mass 50kg
* Crate Underscore: mass 62kg
* Crate Grave: mass 36kg
* Crate a: mass 35kg
* Crate b: mass 60kg
* Crate c: mass 48kg
* Crate d: mass 61kg
* Crate e: mass 59kg
* Crate f: mass 33kg

Each pallet has a maximum safe load capacity of 100 kg. The coordinator must assign every crate to precisely one pallet, ensuring the combined mass on any given pallet does not surpass its limit. The objective is to utilize the smallest possible number of pallets to accommodate the entire shipment.
